name: The Gamboge Wake

detectability.signature: Golden arcs of raw subspace discharge crawling against normal space; broadband noise spikes whenever the bleed surges.

proximity: Sensor ghosts multiply, painting phantom contacts in golden static
Power systems drink greedily, capacitors charging past rated limits
contact: Hull ionization wraps the ship in a glowing corona that scrambles docking and comms
Unshielded electronics fuse as raw hyperspace potential grounds through the vessel
prolonged_exposure: Crew members phase partially into subspace, appearing translucent and speaking with doubled voices
Organic tissue accumulates subspace scarring — numb patches that register on no medical scan

phenomena: Visible plasma discharge arcs in gamboge yellow
Electromagnetic interference patterns rippling outward on each surge
Sensor ghosts and false readings clustering along the bleed front
Hull ionization and corona effects on approaching vessels
hazards: Power system overload burning out drive cores
Radiation exposure exceeding safe limits during surge tides
Dimensional displacement of unshielded crew into shallow subspace layers
opportunities: Energy harvesting potential from the richest raw-subspace source in the sector
Chance to test exotic theories regarding the structure of hyperspace
Emergency escape route — the surge tide masks drive signatures completely
known_incidents: The mining platform Brassy Noon rode a surge tide in 2295 and returned with its crew of forty translucent from the knees down; the platform still runs, largely by itself.
Harvesting consortiums lose on average one tether drone per shift to arcs that strike before the arc exists on sensors.
description: The Gamboge Wake bleeds across normal space in sheets of molten yellow, arcs of raw subspace potential crawling between anchor points no telescope can find. Where the bleed touches dust, the dust glows and forgets its own orbit. On broadband scopes the region roars like a waterfall heard through a wall.

The Wake pulses on a rough nine-hour tide, surging bright and then slackening to a golden haze. Approach too close and sensors drown in phantom contacts while ship capacitors charge hungrily past their limits. At surge peak, arcs leap kilometers to kiss unwary hulls, wrapping them in ionized coronas.

Survey geologists date the bleed to a subspace fault laid down forty million years ago, though no one agrees on what fractured. The platform Brassy Noon moored inside a surge in 2295; her crew walked out translucent from the knee, and the platform has run itself ever since, competently and without complaint. Harvest consortiums now tether drones into the current at enormous profit and regular loss.

Energy cartels maintain floating substations at the tide line, selling bottled Wake-current at prices only navies and cults can pay. The tide masks drive signatures completely, making the Wake the sector's favorite place to disappear. Surge forecasts are posted hourly; they are right about eight hours in nine.
